entry.title: Centre-2026 command post exercise
entry.summary: The Supreme Commander-in-Chief visited the Chebarkul training ground in the Chelyabinsk Region to observe the actions of troops during the active phase of the Centre-2026 command post exercise.
entry.content:
The Supreme Commander-in-Chief visited the Chebarkul training ground in the Chelyabinsk Region to observe the actions of troops during the active phase of the Centre-2026 command post exercise.

The President was accompanied by Defence Minister Andrei Belousov, Presidential Plenipotentiary Envoy to the Ural Federal District Artyom Zhoga, Governor of the Chelyabinsk Region Alexei Teksler, Deputy Defence Minister Yunus-Bek Yevkurov, and Commander-in-Chief of the Ground Forces Andrei Mordvichev.

The strategic exercise is being held from September 28 to October 3 in accordance with the Armed Forces training schedule and is being conducted in conjunction with the CSTO’s Interaction-2026 command post exercise.

Training objectives are being addressed in the Central Asian strategic area and in the waters of the Caspian Sea. The drill involves more than 47,000 military personnel. Seven foreign states have contributed contingents to the exercise, and observers have arrived from 51 countries. More than 6,000 military personnel from Russia and other states, together with units of the CSTO Collective Rapid Reaction Force, are deployed at the Chebarkulsky training ground.

* * *

President of Russia Vladimir Putin: Good afternoon, comrades!

The Centre-2026 command post exercise is being held under the Armed Forces training plan, in conjunction with the Interaction-2026 exercise scheduled as part of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation’s plan.

The drill involves over 47,000 troops who are carrying out missions at 11 training areas as well as in the Caspian Sea. The main objective of the exercise is to improve the skills of commanders at all levels in repelling external aggression. The participants are practising the use of new weapons and military equipment, and all missions are being carried out based on the experience gained during the special military operation.

Today, here at the Chebarkul training ground, we are witnessing the final stage of the Centre-2026 and Interaction-2026 exercises. The active phase involves practical operations by more than 6,000 military personnel from Russia and other countries, as well as units of the CSTO Collective Rapid Reaction Force.

I would like to highlight that delegations from 55 foreign countries have arrived in Russia for these exercises. I would also like to extend a special welcome to the heads and representatives of the foreign defence agencies present here.

I am confident that the results of the Centre-2026 and Interaction-2026 exercises, along with the experience gained by the personnel, will enhance our effectiveness in responding to external threats to our countries’ security.

I would like to ask the Minister of Defence to report on the progress of the final stage of the exercises.

Please, proceed.

Minister of Defence Andrei Belousov: Comrade Supreme Commander-in-Chief,

In accordance with the Russian Armed Forces’ training schedule, the Centre-2026 strategic command post exercise has been underway since September 28.

The exercise involves troops from the Central Military District; formations and units of the Aerospace Forces and Airborne Forces; formations and units under Central Command; and forces of the Caspian Flotilla.

In addition, representatives of nearly 60 countries are participating in the exercise, alongside forces and assets of the CSTO collective security system. Seven countries have deployed military contingents; the defence agency of the Republic of the Congo is represented by an operational group; and 51 countries have sent observers. The total number of troops at the Chebarkul training ground is approximately 6,000. Around 700 pieces of military hardware, more than 600 unmanned aerial vehicles of various types, and over 60 robotic systems are being engaged.

Training objectives are being addressed as part of the operations of the troop grouping in the Central Asian strategic area. The forces have completed their joint preparations and are ready for the active phase of the exercise.

entry.title: Meeting with Governors-Elect
entry.content:
The President held a videoconference with elected heads of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation.

Attending the meeting were Head of Karachayevo-Circassia Rashid Temrezov, Head of the Republic of Mordovia Artyom Zdunov, Head of the Republic North Ossetia–Alania Sergei Menyailo, Head of the Republic of Tuva Vladislav Khovalyg, Head of the Republic of Chechnya Ramzan Kadyrov, Acting Governor of the Belgorod Region Alexander Shuvayev, Governor of the Bryansk Region Yegor Kovalchuk, Governor of the Penza Region Oleg Melnichenko, Governor of the Tver Region Vitaly Korolyov, Governor of the Ulyanovsk Region Alexei Russkikh, and Chief of Staff of the Presidential Executive Office Anton Vaino.

* * *

President of Russia Vladimir Putin: Good afternoon, colleagues.

First of all, congratulations on your victory in the gubernatorial election. I wish you successful work.

I should note that the election was quite competitive. Representatives of different political parties competed for votes; yet, the winners were determined as early as in the first round, by a large margin. Needless to say, this amount of support translates into even greater responsibility. Our citizens essentially rated the results you have already accomplished and indicated their expectation for the continuation of the same course – in the country in general and in their regions, cities and towns.

It is very important that you justify this trust and work with your management teams consistently and to the best your abilities in the interests of the people, always heeding their hopes and wishes, constantly receiving feedback, including through dialogue with all the parties represented in your regional parliaments, and with public and volunteer associations. And of course, the endurance and courage of our fighters engaged in the zone of the special military operation should serve as the primary moral compass for everybody involved in public administration.

Our shared task – one requiring combined efforts from all levels of government, business and civil society – is to further strengthen the country’s sovereignty in the broadest sense of the word.

This encompasses not only defence capabilities and security but also the expansion of our own industrial, scientific and technological competencies, and the creation of conditions for steady and confident socio-economic progress – which in turn drives demographic growth and improves the quality of life for our citizens and Russian families. The mechanisms for achieving these goals are embedded in the national projects, and their successful implementation undoubtedly depends directly on the work being done on the ground, particularly at regional level.

I expect all matters relating to the national projects to remain under your daily supervision. We can achieve these goals only by working together.

In this context, effective interaction with the Government and federal authorities, close coordination between regions, and tight alignment of all regional projects and initiatives with national strategic development plans are of particular importance.

Supporting our military personnel, veterans of the special military operation and their families is of immense moral significance and serves to unite the regions and the people of the entire country. This requires particular sensitivity and attention to every detail and every individual set of circumstances. It is also crucial that those who have demonstrated their finest qualities in combat are able to find fulfilment in civilian life. Relying on such individuals has already become an integral part of personnel policy at all levels of government, aided by relevant training initiatives – specifically, the federal Time of Heroes programme and its regional counterparts.

I would note that, following the recent elections, a participant in this programme – Alexander Shuvayev – was elected Governor of the Belgorod Region. His military experience is of particular importance for this border region.

Personnel initiatives for participants and veterans of the special military operation have already proven their effectiveness and should certainly be expanded, with active support from regional authorities and heads of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Likewise, the mechanisms for medical rehabilitation, employment and legal support for special military operation veterans must be further improved.

It is important that these individuals find meaningful opportunities to apply their skills – whether in state or municipal administration, education, or mentorship roles.

Colleagues,

The country, and the entire governance system, faces tasks of great magnitude. I wish you every success and productive work for the benefit of the country as a whole.

Colleagues, who would like to speak or share information?

Please, go ahead.

<…>

Vladimir Putin: Of course, you all have something to say. But let me stress once again that people came to the polling stations for a reason. They headed to the polls in the hope that everything you have been saying and all the plans for developing your regions you have presented – all this will materialise. You and I will have to shoulder this immense responsibility for promoting national development and reinforcing Russia’s statehood.

I sincerely wish you every success. Let us work together.

All the best!
